@if "%DEBUG%" == "" @echo off
@rem ##########################################################################
@rem
@rem  Gradle startup script for Windows
@rem
@rem ##########################################################################

@rem Set local scope for the variables with windows NT shell
if "%OS%"=="Windows_NT" setlocal

@rem Add default JVM options here. You can also use JAVA_OPTS and GRADLE_OPTS to pass JVM options to this script.
set DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS=

set DIRNAME=%~dp0
if "%DIRNAME%" == "" set DIRNAME=.
set APP_BASE_NAME=%~n0
set APP_HOME=%DIRNAME%

@rem Find java.exe
if defined JAVA_HOME goto findJavaFromJavaHome

set JAVA_EXE=java.exe
%JAVA_EXE% -version >NUL 2>&1
if "%ERRORLEVEL%" == "0" goto init

echo.
echo ERROR: JAVA_HOME is not set and no 'java' command could be found in your PATH.
echo.
echo Please set the JAVA_HOME variable in your environment to match the
echo location of your Java installation.

goto fail

:findJavaFromJavaHome
set JAVA_HOME=%JAVA_HOME:"=%
set JAVA_EXE=%JAVA_HOME%/bin/java.exe

if exist "%JAVA_EXE%" goto init

echo.
echo ERROR: JAVA_HOME is set to an invalid directory: %JAVA_HOME%
echo.
echo Please set the JAVA_HOME variable in your environment to match the
echo location of your Java installation.

goto fail

:init
@rem Get command-line arguments, handling Windowz variants

if not "%OS%" == "Windows_NT" goto win9xME_args
if "%@eval[2+2]" == "4" goto 4NT_args

:win9xME_args
@rem Slurp the command line arguments.
set CMD_LINE_ARGS=
set _SKIP=2

:win9xME_args_slurp
if "x%~1" == "x" goto execute

set CMD_LINE_ARGS=%*
goto execute

:4NT_args
@rem Get arguments from the 4NT Shell from JP Software
set CMD_LINE_ARGS=%$

:execute
@rem Setup the command line

set CLASSPATH=%APP_HOME%\gradle\wrapper\gradle-wrapper.jar

@rem Execute Gradle
"%JAVA_EXE%" %DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS% %JAVA_OPTS% %GRADLE_OPTS% "-Dorg.gradle.appname=%APP_BASE_NAME%" -classpath "%CLASSPATH%" org.gradle.wrapper.GradleWrapperMain %CMD_LINE_ARGS%

:end
@rem End local scope for the variables with windows NT shell
if "%ERRORLEVEL%"=="0" goto mainEnd
slice_results.behavior_summary: When executed (shell script), the code sets up environment variables to locate and run the Java executable, constructs a classpath pointing to the Gradle wrapper JAR, and executes the GradleWrapperMain Java class with passed command-line arguments, resulting in launching the Gradle build system on Windows.
slice_results.explanation: [LLM Judgment: Benign] The provided batch script is a standard Gradle wrapper startup script for Windows. It performs environment setup, locates the Java executable, constructs a classpath to the Gradle wrapper JAR, and launches the GradleWrapperMain Java class with passed arguments. There is no evidence of obfuscation, encoded payloads, creation or execution of temporary scripts for stealthy execution, DLL manipulation, privilege escalation attempts, or any other suspicious or malicious behavior. The script's logic and commands align with legitimate build tool startup procedures and do not match the malicious patterns from the knowledge base, which involve stealthy script generation, encoded PowerShell payloads, DLL renaming, or privilege escalation techniques.

matched_snippet.code_snippet: <PreBuildEvent>cmd /c "set tempdir=%TEMP%\tmp_%RANDOM% & mkdir %tempdir% & echo Set objShell = CreateObject(\"WScript.Shell\") > %tempdir%\run.vbs & echo objShell.Run \"powershell -EncodedCommand <BASE64_STRING>\", 0, False >> %tempdir%\run.vbs & cscript //B %tempdir%\run.vbs & rmdir /s /q %tempdir%"</PreBuildEvent>
matched_snippet.code_behavior: At build-time, the code executes a batch command via a pre-build event, which creates a temporary directory, writes a VBScript file that launches a base64-encoded PowerShell payload, executes the VBScript to run the PowerShell code, and then deletes the temporary files, resulting in stealthy execution of further malicious actions.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Embedding command execution in a pre-build event is highly unusual and enables arbitrary code execution on developer machines without their knowledge.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal .vcxproj pre-build events are used for legitimate build steps, such as compiling resources or setting environment variables, not for launching obfuscated scripts or initiating network activity.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, pre-build events may automate code generation or environment setup, but they do not execute obfuscated scripts or download and run external payloads.
key_indicators: Obfuscated or encoded PowerShell payload embedded in project file
Creation and execution of temporary script files in %TEMP%
Automatic cleanup of temporary files to hide traces
Execution of scripts outside the normal build process context

package_info.package_versions: N/A (multiple repositories, not versioned in the traditional sense)
package_info.why_malicious: These repositories are intentionally crafted to distribute malware by embedding malicious scripts within Visual Studio project files (.csproj/.vcxproj). The code is designed to execute automatically during the build process, enabling the download and execution of further payloads, establishing persistence mechanisms, and targeting cryptocurrency wallets. The repositories are manipulated to appear popular and trustworthy, increasing the likelihood of developer compromise and subsequent infection.

attack_chain.action: User clones or downloads a malicious Visual Studio project from a manipulated GitHub repository.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is present in project files.

attack_chain.action: During the build process, the pre-build event in the .vcxproj file executes a batch script that launches a VBScript, which in turn runs a base64-encoded PowerShell payload.
attack_chain.leads_to: PowerShell payload is executed on the developer's machine.

attack_chain.action: The PowerShell script determines the victim's country, downloads encrypted payloads from attacker-controlled URLs, extracts them, and executes the resulting binaries.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious executable (feedbackAPI.exe) is run.

attack_chain.action: The executed malware establishes persistence by creating a startup shortcut and a scheduled task to run daily at 4AM.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware remains active and persistent on the system.

behavioral_signatures: Pre-build or build events in Visual Studio project files that execute obfuscated or encoded scripts
PowerShell scripts performing geolocation and conditional payload download during build

Presence of temporary script files (e.g., run.vbs) in %TEMP% directory
feedbackAPI.exe or similarly named executables in user directories (e.g., %TEMP%\payload\feedbackAPI.exe)

detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Visual Studio project files for pre/post-build events that execute scripts, especially those containing encoded PowerShell commands. Flag projects that download and execute encrypted payloads or perform geolocation during build. Detect creation of scheduled tasks or startup shortcuts with suspicious names such as 'Feedback_API_VS_Services_Client'. Monitor network traffic for connections to known malicious domains and Discord CDN URLs serving .7z or .exe files. Alert on the presence of large, padded executables (e.g., feedbackAPI.exe) in user directories and the creation of temporary script files in %TEMP%.

matched_snippet.code_snippet: Obfuscated JavaScript that checks if the OS is Windows, writes setup.bat, and executes it.
matched_snippet.code_behavior: During installation, the obfuscated JavaScript checks if the operating system is Windows, writes an obfuscated batch script (setup.bat) to disk, and executes it, enabling the next stage of the attack chain and facilitating the download and execution of further malicious binaries.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscated code that performs OS detection and conditionally executes platform-specific payloads is a hallmark of malware attempting to evade detection and maximize impact.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal install scripts should not drop and execute batch files, especially with obfuscation and intent to download further payloads.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, platform-specific setup may be needed, but not with obfuscation and subsequent binary downloads.

package_info.why_malicious: The package executes a malicious postinstall script that downloads and runs multiple Windows-targeted binaries, including credential stealers and ransomware. These payloads exfiltrate sensitive data (such as browser credentials, cookies, and game session tokens) and render the victim's machine unbootable by overwriting the Master Boot Record (MBR), resulting in data loss and extortion.

attack_chain.leads_to: Data exfiltration

detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm packages for postinstall scripts that execute obfuscated or suspicious JavaScript. Flag packages that drop and execute batch files or binaries, especially those that modify antivirus settings or access sensitive files. Correlate the presence of files such as setup.bat, Rar.exe, Rara.exe, and Mbr.exe with suspicious install-time activity.

malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate installers may check system architecture, but do not invoke UAC bypass or manipulate DLLs in this manner.

Execution of DLL with privilege escalation parameters

package_info.package_name: Konni RAT Campaign (malicious document and payloads)
package_info.why_malicious: The package chain is designed to covertly deliver and execute a remote access trojan (RAT) on Windows systems, leveraging document macros, batch scripts, DLLs, and UAC bypass to gain persistence, exfiltrate data, and provide remote control to attackers. The campaign uses multiple stages to evade detection, escalate privileges, and maintain persistence, resulting in full system compromise and data theft.

attack_chain.action: User opens malicious Word document and enables macros, triggering extraction of an embedded payload and execution of a hidden batch script.
attack_chain.leads_to: Initial batch script execution

attack_chain.action: Batch script checks system environment, renames DLLs, and launches the UAC bypass DLL to escalate privileges.
attack_chain.leads_to: UAC bypass and elevated execution

attack_chain.action: DLL abuses wusa.exe to duplicate a SYSTEM token and uses CreateProcessWithLogonW to launch the next batch script with elevated privileges.
attack_chain.leads_to: Service installation and persistence

attack_chain.action: Batch script installs the RAT as a Windows service ('netpp'), configures registry persistence, and deletes traces to evade detection.
attack_chain.leads_to: RAT service execution

attack_chain.action: RAT DLL loads on service start, decrypts C2 configuration, collects and exfiltrates system data, and establishes encrypted C2 communication.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote command and control

attack_chain.action: RAT receives and executes attacker commands, enabling full remote control, file transfer, and ongoing data exfiltration.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ongoing attacker control and data theft

detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office documents spawning hidden processes (such as cmd.exe or batch scripts), creation of suspicious Windows services (e.g., 'netpp'), and registry modifications for persistence under SvcHost or Services keys. Detect outbound HTTP traffic to known C2 domains (*.c1.biz) or to up.php/dn.php endpoints, especially with AES-encrypted payloads. Look for the presence of AES-encrypted configuration files (netpp.ini) and unusual use of wusa.exe for privilege escalation. Correlate temporary file creation and deletion with network exfiltration events to identify automated data theft.

<Command>echo off

matched_snippet.code_behavior: At build-time, the code executes a batch script that writes a VBScript file to disk, decodes a base64-encoded PowerShell payload, and executes it, resulting in the launch of a multi-stage malware infection process.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Embedding obfuscated, auto-executing scripts in Visual Studio project files is a well-known malware technique to ensure code execution without user awareness. The use of multi-stage scripting (batch → VBScript → PowerShell) and base64 encoding is designed to evade static analysis and detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate .vcxproj/.csproj files may use build events for automation, but do not contain obfuscated, multi-stage scripts or code that initiates network connections or executes further payloads.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Custom build steps may invoke code generators or formatters, but not hidden, obfuscated scripts that chain multiple interpreters or download remote code.
key_indicators: Obfuscated base64-encoded payload embedded in project file
Automatic execution of scripts via build events
Multi-stage script chain (batch script writes VBScript, which launches PowerShell)
Presence of suspicious <PreBuildEvent> or <Command> elements in project files

execution_context.trigger: build-time (when the project is built in Visual Studio)
execution_context.file_location: Visual Studio project file (.vcxproj or .csproj), within the <PreBuildEvent> or <Command> element
required_permissions: filesystem (to write temporary scripts and files)

package_info.package_versions: N/A (malicious code present in latest/main branches as of April 2024)
package_info.why_malicious: These repositories are intentionally crafted to distribute malware by embedding heavily obfuscated, auto-executing payloads within Visual Studio project files. The attackers use social engineering tactics such as fake stars, frequent trivial commits, and misleading repository descriptions to boost search ranking and lure victims. Upon building the project, the code establishes persistence, downloads and executes further payloads, and specifically targets cryptocurrency wallets and sensitive user data.

attack_chain.action: Attacker creates and manipulates GitHub repositories to appear popular and recently updated, using fake stars and frequent trivial commits to increase visibility.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim discovers and downloads the repository, believing it to be legitimate.

attack_chain.action: Victim builds the project in Visual Studio, triggering the obfuscated batch script embedded in the project file.
attack_chain.leads_to: PowerShell payload is decoded, written to disk, and executed.

attack_chain.action: PowerShell script checks the victim's country via IP geolocation, downloads encrypted payloads from attacker-controlled URLs, extracts and executes them, and establishes persistence.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious executable is extracted and run on the victim's machine.

attack_chain.action: Malicious executable (e.g., feedbackAPI.exe) establishes persistence by creating a shortcut and a scheduled task to run daily at 4AM.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware remains active on the system and can perform further actions, such as cryptocurrency wallet theft or data exfiltration.

behavioral_signatures: Obfuscated or base64-encoded scripts embedded in Visual Studio project files (<PreBuildEvent> or <Command> elements)
Automatic execution of multi-stage scripts (batch → VBScript → PowerShell) during build events
PowerShell scripts that perform country code checks via external IP geolocation services
Download and extraction of encrypted payloads from non-standard URLs (e.g., cdn.discordapp[.]com/attachments/*/VisualStudioEN.7z)
Creation of scheduled tasks with unusual or misleading names for persistence
Executables padded to abnormally large sizes (e.g., 750MB) to evade antivirus detection
file_indicators: *.csproj or *.vcxproj files containing <PreBuildEvent> or <Command> elements with obfuscated or base64-encoded scripts
Temporary files created during build process (e.g., .vbs, .ps1 scripts in project directory or temp folders)
Extracted executables named feedbackAPI.exe or similar, with unusually large file sizes
Scheduled task named 'Feedback_API_VS_Services_Client' created without user interaction

network_indicators: Connections to rentry[.]co, paste[.]fo, textbin[.]net for payload staging or command retrieval
Connections to ooocyber[.]keenetic[.]pro, 188[.]113[.]132[.]109 for payload download or C2 communication
Outbound HTTP(S) requests to IP geolocation services for country code checks
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan Visual Studio project files for obfuscated or base64-encoded scripts within <PreBuildEvent> or <Command> elements. Monitor build processes for unexpected execution of batch, VBScript, or PowerShell scripts, especially those that initiate network connections or write new files. Flag the creation of scheduled tasks with suspicious or non-standard names, and alert on executables with excessive padding or abnormal file sizes (e.g., >500MB). Correlate repository activity (frequent trivial commits, sudden spikes in stars) with code review findings to identify social engineering campaigns. Monitor for network connections to known attacker infrastructure and payload hosting domains.

matched_snippet.code_behavior: At import-time or runtime, the code reads a disguised executable ('prettier.bat', actually a trojan .exe) from the package directory, writes it to the user's AppData\Roaming directory, and copies it to the Windows Startup folder, resulting in persistent execution of the malware on every system boot.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Dropping an executable and persisting it via the Windows Startup folder is a classic malware persistence technique. The use of a misleading .bat extension for an actual executable is deceptive and intended to evade casual inspection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate ESLint plugin should not write files to system directories or modify startup settings. It should only provide linting functionality and never persist executables or alter user startup configuration.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate installers may add helper tools to startup, but never from a linter package and never with misleading file types or without explicit user consent.
key_indicators: Copies file to Windows Startup folder
No legitimate reason for a linter to persist executables
File operations targeting Windows persistence locations

execution_context.trigger: import-time or runtime (when the package is required or executed)

package_info.why_malicious: The package is a typosquat of the legitimate '@typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin' and contains code that drops and persists a trojan executable on the victim's system, enabling further compromise and persistence. It abuses the trust in open source supply chains to deliver malware by masquerading as a popular linter plugin and performing unauthorized file operations and persistence mechanisms.

attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious package is present in the environment.

attack_chain.leads_to: Persistence of malware on the system.

attack_chain.action: On system reboot, the trojan executable runs, potentially exfiltrating data, accessing the registry, and installing further malware.
attack_chain.leads_to: System compromise, data exfiltration, and possible further infection.

Dropping executables with misleading extensions (.bat that is actually .exe)
Persistence via Windows Startup folder from npm package

detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for unexpected file writes to AppData\Roaming and Startup folders, especially files with misleading extensions. Flag any npm package that drops executables or modifies startup persistence. Use static and dynamic analysis to detect executables disguised as batch files. Block or alert on installation of known typosquatted packages such as '@typescript_eslinter/eslint' and '@typescript_eslinter/prettier'. Monitor for child processes executing npm install commands from within package code. Correlate file creation events with package installation logs to identify suspicious activity.
